ruling.recommended_action: Issue a Ryde voucher of $4.17 to the rider for the unexempted off-route segment's distance units, and record the driver's RD-1 breach (first route dispute, no account flag) on the trip file. No voucher for the 0.24 km residual or the time component.

segment_findings.reason: One off-route segment 09:32–09:38 adding 2.96 km and straying up to 974 m from the optimal route [F3]. Not exempted by RD-3 (no rider-named stop or rider routing request [F7]), not exempted by RD-4(a) (no incident near the route in the trip window [F11]) or RD-4(b) (only band 4, above band 1/2; corroboration only [F9][F10][F12]), and not exempted by RD-5 (no prior driver request + rider agreement — no chat at all [F7][F8]). It is therefore an unexempted detour under RD-1 and its extra_km is refundable under RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's reasonable-cause exemption fails: no traffic incident near the route during the trip window [F11][RD-4](a), and the band 4 speed records on East Coast Parkway and Airport Boulevard are neither band 1 nor band 2 and cannot exempt on their own [F9][F10][RD-4](b).

Rejected: fair weather at 0.0 mm rain [F12] and band 4 traffic [F9][F10] are the opposite of the reasonable cause RD-4 requires, and the longer duration [F2] shows only that the trip took longer, not that the 2.96 km deviation was justified [RD-4].

Rejected as to the absence of consent cutting both ways: RD-5 excuses a segment only when the driver proposed the change and the rider agreed before leaving the optimal route; with no chat at all [F7] and a statement that yields to the GPS record [F8][F3], no consent exists and the segment remains unexempted [RD-5].

Rejected insofar as the driver disputes that the whole segment's extra_km is refundable: RD-2 refunds the extra_km of the unexempted segment, and F3 fixes that at 2.96 km, giving 2.96 × $1.41 = $4.17 [F3][F6][RD-2].

Rejected as to characterising the 0.24 km residual as no driver conduct at all; the residual is simply not refundable under RD-2, while the 2.96 km segment itself is an unexempted deviation under RD-1 [F1][F3][RD-2].
Accepted only in part: the +3.2 km headline is not the refund base; RD-2 limits recovery to the unexempted segment's 2.96 km, leaving the ~0.24 km residual unrefunded [F1][F3][F4][RD-2].

Partially rejected: the $4.17 distance refund is granted, but no part of the $12.96 time charge or the +21.4 min over-run is recoverable because RD-2 refunds only the distance unit of unexempted segments [F2][F6][RD-2].
Accepted: with 0 upheld route disputes in the 90-day profile, the RD-6 repeated-breach precondition is unmet and no account flag attaches [F14][RD-6].
